item.title: Children aged 3 to 5 account for largest share of suspected abuse victims: NGO
item.description: Children aged three to five accounted for the largest share of victims among 216 suspected child abuse cases recorded over the past financial year by a Hong Kong group, which attributed the trend to heavy pressure on parents and insufficient parenting skills. Physical abuse made up about half of the cases, followed by neglect, psychological abuse, sexual abuse and multiple forms of abuse. item.title: Houthis hit Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper in strike on Saudi wealth fund HQ
item.description: Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper, headquarters of the Saudi sovereign wealth fund, was struck on Thursday by a suspected Houthi missile in the latest blow in the Iran-backed Yemeni group’s war with the kingdom. The strike blew out windows across seven to eight floors of PIF Tower, bending parts of its metal facade. item.title: Abby Choi’s ex-husband tells trial of love triangle, romance and sex until her death
item.description: Slain Hong Kong socialite Abby Choi Tin-fung’s ex-husband has told a court they were in a “complicated” relationship, noting that they had remained romantically and sexually involved after their divorce and up until her death. item.title: China’s abundant electricity is not yet a decisive AI edge
item.description: As Washington continues to tighten controls over advanced chip exports, China faces greater obstacles to accessing high-performance processors. The fall of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, a prominent advocate for selling chips to China, adds another layer of uncertainty. item.title: Japanese PM Takaichi tries to break ice with Xi by thanking him for hosting Apec summit
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi thanked Chinese President Xi Jinping for inviting her to the Apec summit and congratulated him on successfully hosting the event on Thursday. Speaking at a press conference at the end of her visit to Shenzhen, Takaichi described her brief interactions with the Chinese leader.
